mcqs.question: A student thinks that the coefficient of friction is the same whether the surfaces are moving relative to each other or not. Which statement correctly identifies the misconception?

options.A: The coefficient of static friction is always smaller than the coefficient of kinetic friction.
options.B: The coefficient of static friction and kinetic friction are equal for a given pair of surfaces.
options.C: The coefficient of static friction is generally larger than the coefficient of kinetic friction.
options.D: The coefficient of friction does not depend on the nature of the surfaces.

mcqs.answer: The coefficient of static friction is generally larger than the coefficient of kinetic friction.
mcqs.explanation: For any pair of surfaces, the coefficient of static friction (μs) is usually greater than the coefficient of kinetic friction (μk). μs represents the maximum friction before motion starts, while μk is the friction during sliding. Option C states this correctly; the other options either reverse the relationship or ignore surface dependence.

mcqs.question: A 5 kg block rests on a rough incline making an angle of 30° with the horizontal. The coefficient of static friction is 0.5. Which reasoning correctly explains whether the block will start sliding?

options.A: The component of weight down the plane (24.5 N) is less than the maximum static friction (21.2 N), so the block remains at rest.
options.B: The component of weight down the plane (24.5 N) exceeds the maximum static friction (21.2 N), so the block starts sliding.
options.C: The normal reaction on an inclined plane is zero, making friction zero; therefore the block slides.
options.D: Friction always prevents motion regardless of the weight component, so the block will not slide.

mcqs.answer: The component of weight down the plane (24.5 N) exceeds the maximum static friction (21.2 N), so the block starts sliding.
mcqs.explanation: Weight component down the incline = mg sin θ = 5 × 9.8 × 0.5 = 24.5 N. Normal reaction = mg cos θ = 5 × 9.8 × 0.866 ≈ 42.4 N. Maximum static friction = μs N = 0.5 × 42.4 ≈ 21.2 N. Since 24.5 N > 21.2 N, the block overcomes static friction and begins to slide. Option B captures this reasoning; the others are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares static friction and kinetic friction for a block moving on a rough surface?

options.A: Static friction is always equal to kinetic friction for the same pair of surfaces.
options.B: Static friction can take any value up to its maximum, whereas kinetic friction has a constant value equal to μk N.
options.C: Kinetic friction is always greater than static friction because the surfaces are already in motion.
options.D: Both static and kinetic friction are independent of the normal reaction.

mcqs.answer: Static friction can take any value up to its maximum, whereas kinetic friction has a constant value equal to μk N.
mcqs.explanation: Static friction adjusts itself to match the applied force up to a maximum value μs N. Once motion starts, kinetic friction acts with a fixed magnitude μk N, independent of the applied force. Therefore option B is correct; the other options misrepresent the relationship or ignore the role of the normal reaction.

mcqs.question: A crate is pulled across a horizontal floor with constant speed. Which statement about the forces of static and kinetic friction acting on the crate is true?

options.A: Both static and kinetic friction act simultaneously, each equal to half the applied force.
options.B: Static friction acts to oppose motion, while kinetic friction is zero because the speed is constant.
options.C: Kinetic friction equals the applied force, and static friction is zero because the crate is moving.
options.D: Neither static nor kinetic friction is present when the crate moves at constant speed.

mcqs.answer: Kinetic friction equals the applied force, and static friction is zero because the crate is moving.
mcqs.explanation: When an object moves at constant velocity, the net horizontal force is zero. The applied force is balanced by kinetic friction (μk N). Static friction only acts when there is a tendency to start moving; once the crate is already sliding, static friction is absent. Hence option C correctly describes the situation.

mcqs.question: What is the term used for the maximum value of static friction that can act before motion starts?
mcqs.explanation: The greatest possible static friction before slipping occurs is called limiting friction. It equals μs N. Kinetic friction acts after motion begins, while rolling and adhesive frictions are different phenomena.

mcqs.question: A block of weight 50 N rests on a horizontal surface. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the surface is 0.2. What is the magnitude of the kinetic friction force acting on the block?
mcqs.explanation: Kinetic friction = μk N = 0.2 × 50 N = 10 N. Option B gives the correct value; the other options result from incorrect multiplication or omission of the coefficient.

mcqs.question: Which definition correctly describes the coefficient of friction?

options.A: Ratio of the frictional force to the normal reaction between two surfaces.
options.B: Ratio of the normal reaction to the frictional force.
options.C: The absolute value of the frictional force irrespective of the normal force.
options.D: The product of the frictional force and the normal reaction.

mcqs.answer: Ratio of the frictional force to the normal reaction between two surfaces.
mcqs.explanation: The coefficient of friction (μ) is defined as μ = F_friction / N, where N is the normal reaction. Option A states this definition accurately; the other options invert or misrepresent the relationship.

mcqs.question: A 2 kg block is placed on a rough incline that makes an angle of 20° with the horizontal. The coefficient of static friction is 0.4. Will the block remain at rest?

options.A: Yes, because the maximum static friction (7.36 N) exceeds the component of weight down the plane (6.7 N).
options.B: No, because the component of weight down the plane (6.7 N) exceeds the maximum static friction (7.36 N).
options.C: The block will oscillate back and forth on the incline.
options.D: There is insufficient information to decide.

mcqs.answer: Yes, because the maximum static friction (7.36 N) exceeds the component of weight down the plane (6.7 N).
mcqs.explanation: Weight component down the incline = mg sin θ = 2 × 9.8 × sin20° ≈ 6.7 N. Normal reaction = mg cos θ ≈ 18.4 N. Maximum static friction = μs N = 0.4 × 18.4 ≈ 7.36 N. Since 6.7 N < 7.36 N, static friction can hold the block, so it stays at rest. Option A correctly states this; the other options are incorrect.
